safety.en: The seafront felt comfortable early on, while busier shared paths later made faster sessions less convenient.

scenery.en: Sunrise, ocean views, palms and nearby hills made the scenery a 10/10 for me.

surface.en: Paved coastal paths for road sessions, with short rises and rocky trails nearby for a change of terrain.

access.en: It is easy to choose a shorter, fairly flat stretch or a longer outing, with more room early in the morning.

experience.en: I have returned several times, done easy runs, intervals and hill sessions, and would gladly come back again.

en.title: Tenerife: Los Cristianos to La Caleta
en.excerpt: Sunrise runs, surfers and a long seafront linking Los Cristianos, Las Américas, Costa Adeje and La Caleta. One of the places I keep returning to.
en.body:
Sunrise on this coast has the same kind of magic I associate with Rome. The light, the sea and the first runners heading along the promenade make getting out of bed early feel like a very good decision.

My visits have been in October and November, so the warmth I describe here is from those autumn trips. I have been back several times now, and I will go again. Between Los Cristianos, Playa de las Américas, Costa Adeje and La Caleta, I have managed easy jogs, intervals and hill sessions, all with views I would happily give 10/10.

## A long seafront, with options for different runs

I think of this as roughly 10 km of coastal running to explore in one direction, depending on the exact path and detours you choose. That is a rough guide to the stretch, rather than the distance of every run. My longer recorded outing below covers 23.2 km in total, going along the coast and back.

There are hills if you want them, but you do not have to make every run a climbing session. I have also been able to put together around 6 km of fairly flat running by the sea. For a relaxed jog, I would pick one of those easier stretches and turn around whenever it suited me.

![Runners on a broad paved path beside the sea and palm trees](/assets/uploads/tenerife-south-coast/morning-seafront-runners.jpg "Room to settle into a pace along the coast in the morning.")

Around Las Américas, you get surfers as well as runners. That mix gives the place a nice morning atmosphere. There is also a surf bar I like where runners stop for coffee afterwards. I cannot give you a reliable name for it here, but that post-run coffee by the sea is part of what I enjoy about coming back.

## Go early

Morning would be my clear recommendation. There are fewer people wandering across the promenade, more runners around you and much more room to settle into a pace.

Later on, the same path becomes a shared holiday promenade. That is perfectly nice for a stroll, but less convenient for intervals or a steady run. I would save the faster sessions for a quieter time and stay considerate around walkers.

![Palm trees and walkers beside the sea on the Los Cristianos promenade](/assets/uploads/tenerife-south-coast/palm-lined-promenade.jpg "The waterfront is shared with people out for a walk, especially later in the day.")

## What the longer route shows

The GPX follows the coastal area through Los Cristianos and Las Américas, north through Costa Adeje towards La Caleta, and back again. It is a longer outing with small changes of direction, rather than a perfectly straight promenade run.

The recorded line has approximately 190 m of accumulated climbing, with elevations ranging from roughly 7 to 44 m above sea level. The profile shows a longer rise around the 5 km mark, some shorter ups and downs farther along the Costa Adeje and La Caleta side, and another rise around 17 to 18 km on the return. Those distances refer to this particular recording, so use the shape of the route and the profile together when choosing a section.

![Elevation profile of the 23.2 km Tenerife coastal run, showing short climbs and flatter stretches](/assets/uploads/tenerife-south-coast/elevation-profile.svg "Distance and elevation from my GPX. Elevation gain is an estimate, with small recording fluctuations filtered out.")

For accommodation, somewhere between Las Américas and Los Cristianos would be my personal starting point. I like having the seafront close by and being able to choose which direction to run. The map should help you decide which section would suit your own training better.

![A blue-railed pedestrian bridge overlooking the marina and coast in early light](/assets/uploads/tenerife-south-coast/coastal-footbridge.jpg "Another view from the coast on one of my visits.")

## There are trails above Los Cristianos too

It is not all pavement. The rocky hills beside Los Cristianos give trail runners another option, with a very different feel from the promenade.

The Montaña de Guaza area, between Los Cristianos and Palm-Mar, is worth looking into if you want to leave the seafront behind. [Tenerife’s official tourism page](https://www.webtenerife.co.uk/what-see/outdoor-attractions/montana-guaza/) has information about the protected landscape. The photo below is from the hills by Los Cristianos; it gives you an idea of the terrain without promising that every trail is equally easy to run.

![Rocky hills above Los Cristianos with a view towards the surrounding mountains at sunrise](/assets/uploads/tenerife-south-coast/los-cristianos-hills.jpg "The hills above Los Cristianos offer a different kind of outing from the paved waterfront.")

## Warm weather, but check for Calima

The warmth is a big part of the appeal. Tenerife’s [mild coastal winters](https://www.webtenerife.co.uk/tenerife/climatology/) make it an attractive place to escape colder-weather training.

Check the air quality as well as the temperature. Calima brings airborne dust, and a bad episode is a reason to change the plan. I check the air-quality reading in my weather app; the [Canary Islands government advises against strenuous exercise during Calima](https://www.gobiernodecanarias.org/emergencias/alertas/consejos/calima/calima.html).

## A run club I still need to try

I tried contacting [De Costa Run Club](https://www.instagram.com/decosta.runclub/), but did not hear back and never managed to join a session. That is simply my experience of trying to arrange it, so I cannot give a first-hand review of their runs.

If you have joined them, know another local group, or spot something here that needs changing, send me a message on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/markuskaljuste/) or [Strava](https://strava.app.link/W1a7SCITG7b). I would be happy to add useful local knowledge.

For me, this is very close to a 10/10 running destination. Easy coastal kilometres, somewhere to run faster, hills when I want them and trails nearby. I keep finding reasons to return.
